target_customer: Self funded drug discovery programs, with pharma partners as future licensees and collaborators
problem: Many gene regulators such as transcription factors are called undruggable because their proteins fail to function in artificial screening systems. Talus built a platform to screen drugs in live human cells and measure effects on the whole regulome at once.
business_model: Biotech drug discovery with pipeline programs and partnership or out-licensing revenue
product_category: AI enabled regulome drug discovery platform (proteomics and automated cell processing)

founders.name: Alex Federation
education: Trained with Jay Bradner at Harvard in medicinal chemistry and drug screening (per YC page; no degree listed)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he later moved to Seattle for training in epigenomics and proteomics.

founders.name: Lindsay Pino
education: Trained at the Broad Institute, University of Washington and University of Pennsylvania (per YC page; no degree listed)
founders.background_notes: Focus on quantitative proteomics at scale.

technical_complexity.rationale: Requires automated live cell processing, next generation proteomics and analytics to measure transcription factor activity in unmodified human cells, which is research grade work.

defensibility.rationale: A hard to replicate wet lab plus proteomics platform and growing screening data, but the end value depends on drug candidates and IP not yet proven.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent is documented as copying or buying the company; in Dec 2025 it announced a collaboration with PRISM BioLab.

market_need_then: Transcription factors and other gene regulators were widely described as undruggable, and the YC page frames moving discovery out of artificial systems into live cells as the solution.

brand_strength.rationale: Only a third party profile reads the name as a bone and a rock slope; the company has no documented brand assets and the name is shared with unrelated firms such as Talus Holdings.

outcome_analysis: Talus Bio started on small federal grants and pre-seed money, raised a 9.75 million dollar seed in 2022 and an 11.2 million dollar Seed+ led by Two Bear Capital in August 2024. It is still active, adding hires and a 2025 collaboration, with no exit yet; the research grade platform keeps outcomes uncertain.
